**Performance: PASS WITH NOTES** at `a8a5758702ce7208172f8af6d635c458dc754b43`.

Delta from `26d2df93dba7bb02dbaf7829928875c52d8961b3`, cost output `eae4679d97fee9301a849cd09239e2bb15667890`. The single intervening commit adds independent randomness at each existing prime-FYI hold, plus its test/docs. P189-F001/F002 remain closed; holder selection, indexed own/owner reads, conditional mark, migration 0046 and partial-index append costs are unchanged.

**Incremental budget:** let D be the existing deduplicated recipient count for a winning nudge: distinct live designated primes, or at most one fallback parent. There are **D extra calls to `occurrence()`**, each filling 16 random bytes and collecting 32 lowercase hex characters. The existing helper also creates sixteen short `format!` String intermediates per successful fill before collecting the final String. This adds bounded encoding/allocation work and a synchronous OS-entropy operation per recipient, not a new process or data-store read.

The nudge still spends one existing mint before its mark attempt, including vetoed attempts. Only a winning mark reaches the FYI loop; each of its D recipients then gets its own mint, even if the owner's delivery was refused or that FYI hold later fails. Successful fills therefore request 16 x (1 + D) bytes for that winning occurrence. No fresh randomness is spent by already-marked holders on later ticks. Over a tick, the added call count is the sum of D over winning nudges, not every seat or every idle-holder lookup.

A failed FYI mint skips body/id construction and `hold_fyi` for that prime, converts the error into its existing outcome/audit entry, and continues with the other primes. It does not add a separate audit append, retry loop or writer commit. The mark already records the one attempt, so that failed prime is not retried within the same idle stretch. This new RNG-error branch is source-reviewed, not fault-injected in the supplied regression.

No new timer, poll, sweep, store/network query, executable site or notification recipient is added. The existing 60-second watchdog round and one owner attempt plus D FYIs remain. Entropy latency is not measured or given a hard deadline; fixed byte count is not a hard wall-clock bound. Existing project/live-seat scans, holding-label preparation, FYI storage/delivery and the index/migration costs remain as priced in the prior verdict.

**Exact-head CI:** [42495647410](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42495647410), attempt 1, successful Rust job `128777285138`, upload artifact **13623159044**. Artifact metadata pins the full head; JUnit shows **2,248 executed cases passed**, zero failures/errors/skips, with five separately skipped by nextest. Verified the new two-prime case, all eight daemon idle-nudge cases and six spawn guards. The new case checks independent 32-character parts; the reviewed helper produces hex with `02x`. Rust lint, Node22/24 and replacement delivers checks succeed. The two new mutants are author-reported, not rerun.

Detached shared worktree and GitHub heads agree, clean and CLEAN. No local build, test, mutation, query-plan benchmark or live probe. The feature-off baseline in `eae4679` is unchanged; a matched after-deploy spawn/CPU/RSS reading remains owed. This cost verdict does not clear correctness/security.
